ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories against FATF-required PEP lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions and OFAC SDN/SSI lists before notarization. Enhanced due diligence under CSSF Circulars (as amended) applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk third-country nationals and client funding routed through high-risk or shell jurisdictions. Evidence of screening must be recorded in the AML/CFT file for five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use the Latin alphabet; non-Roman character names are transliterated into the official Latin script and reproduced phonetically in the articles. The name must be distinguishable from all existing RCS entries and from all reserved names. A Luxembourg SARL must contain 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviations 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL'. The notary verifies uniqueness and local-language translation during the incorporation deed; any French/German/Luxembourgish text is controlling over foreign translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the notary or applicant must within five business days request a written statement of the LBR/RCS registrar. If rejection is maintained, file a reasoned objection to the Minister of Justice within fifteen days from the notification. A further appeal lies to the Luxembourg administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif). Competing third-party objections based on trademarks or company law rights are handled through opposition before the IPIL / LBR before incorporation; if time is critical, an applicant may apply to the President of the District Court for summary relief (mesure provisoire) to order the registrar to state the cause and preserve the reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address cannot satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement for an SARL that will carry on regulated study-abroad and visa consultancy. The company must have a real and stable seat in Luxembourg where the commercial books and AML files are kept, and where competent authorities can serve process. A commercial domiciliation company may provide the address only if it provides a physical serviced room and restricted access to the file; a pure mail-forwarding or virtual-office address is impermissible for this licensed industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 60% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a licensed SARL holding client funds in escrow; higher if the registered office appears to be a passive domiciliation or if the RBE shows rapid changes of UBOs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies and Associations, as amended by the Laws of 10 August 2016 and 19 August 2024, Articles 710-1 to 710-28 (legal form SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and on annual accounts; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Luxembourg Business Registers; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 July 2019 on RCS fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 14 rue Erasme, L-1468 Luxembourg; electronic filing through the e-RCS portal at lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial acte de constitution (public deed of incorporation) executed by a Luxembourg notary and filed electronically by the notary via the e-RCS platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital EUR 12,000; each share must be fully subscribed; at least 25% (EUR 3,000) of cash contributions must be paid up on incorporation and deposited in a blocked escrow account of a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank issues an attestation de blocage to the notary; in-kind contributions require an independent auditor's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION
1. Share Subscription: the entire EUR 12,000 share capital is subscribed in cash by the founder.
2. Capital Blocking: EUR 3,000 (25%) is deposited in the Luxembourg blocked escrow account; the bank certificate is remitted to the notary.
3. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; the manager is authorised to execute the lease and notify the RCS.
4. Officer Appointment: [Name], Luxembourg resident, is appointed sole manager (gérant) with full authority to bind the company, including banking and RCS formalities.
5. Publications: the manager shall complete RCS registration, RESA publication and tax registrations.
This Resolution is immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name search and drafting of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS index portal of Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu); drafting coordinated by the Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a full-text search in the RCS database to confirm that the proposed corporate name is available and distinguishable; fix the legal form as SARL; instruct the notary to draft the statuts including corporate purpose, share capital, registered office, managers' powers and duration; verify the manager's good character and Luxembourg residence; obtain the landlord's written consent for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and RCS search result
Draft articles of association (statuts) prepared by the notary
Identity documents, address and nationality of all shareholders
Curriculum vitae and residence certificate of the designated manager
Landlord consent letter for use of premises as registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS search identifies a conflicting or misleading name, submit a corrective denomination and re-run the search; a new search is performed without substantive state fee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; electronic access via MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: On incorporation the SARL is registered in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS-LBR) and is automatically attributed a matricule (national registration number, e.g. B123456). The company must then file VAT registration form 641 with the AEDT within 15 days of the first taxable transaction to obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number formatted LU + 8 digits. Non-EU entities performing taxable supplies in Luxembourg must appoint a VAT representative approved by the AEDT; EU entities may register directly. The VAT ID application requires the certificate of incorporation, minutes of appointment of the day-to-day manager, articles of association, proof of business address and, for non-residents, a power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A SARL is a resident corporate vehicle fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax on worldwide income (statutory seat or central administration in Luxembourg). It is not transparent for CIT purposes and cannot elect pass-through treatment; the territorial scope covers worldwide profits, relieved only by applicable tax treaties, the participation exemption (Article 166 LIR) and the 80% net-wealth-tax reduction for qualified participations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections are available. Elective mechanisms that do exist: (i) option for a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT law; (ii) participation-exemption elections under Article 166 LIR and dividends-received deduction; (iii) R&D super-deduction election (Articles 50 bis and 57 LIR); (iv) option to apply the special IP box regime of Article 50 ter LIR (80% exemption of qualifying IP income); and (v) ATAD-2 anti-hybrid rules (Article 168 septdecies LIR) which automatically neutralise mismatches with no taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-established suppliers - registration is due from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. An established SARL may benefit from the small-business franchise exemption only if its annual turnover stays at or below EUR 35,000; above EUR 35,000 the company must register and collect VAT at the standard rate. Placement and immigration consultancy fees are standard-rated (B2B Luxembourg/B2C supplies) unless the place of supply is outside Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate or digital stamping system for B2B VAT. E-invoicing is accepted, B2G transmissions must use the PEPPOL network, invoices must be issued within one month of the supply, and VAT returns (module TVA) are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu on a monthly/quarterly calendar. Taxpayers must retain source files, the eCDF customer data file and all supporting documentation for six years to support electronic audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to exports physically dispatched outside the EU within 90 days of supply, provided the exporter holds conclusive evidence of exit (Article 55 VAT law). Services: cross-border consulting, study-abroad and visa-advisory services supplied to a non-EU B2B customer are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (zero-effective) where the customer is established outside the EU and the place-of-supply rule of Article 45(1) VAT Directive applies; for EU B2B customers the supply is taxable in the recipient's country under reverse charge. B2C services to non-EU clients remain taxable in Luxembourg at 17% unless the use-and-enjoyment rule (Article 46 bis VAT law) shifts the place of supply to the country of use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ECS - EX form) lodged via the Luxembourg customs electronic portal
Transport evidence in an unbroken chain: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note signed by the consignee outside the EU
Commercial invoice, purchase order, contract and payment evidence (Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103) matching the VAT return
For services: ECOFS (European Community Output Form explanatory note), non-EU VAT registration certificate of the customer and due-diligence file confirming the B2B place of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively claw back zero-rated VAT together with late interest at 0.6% per month and a 10% penalty if export evidence, ECOFS or VIES statements are missing or inaccurate; penalties escalate to 100% of the tax in fraud cases with criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment between 8 days and 5 years. The statute of limitations is 3 years for genuine errors and 10 years for fraudulent or intentionally concealed operations; the AEDT regularly issues e-audit requests on export files, and the burden of proof rests on the taxable dealer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential and AML supervision: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area jurisdiction; the euro is fully convertible and capital movements are liberalised under Articles 63-66 TFEU. No exchange-control or capital-account authorisation regime exists for current or capital transactions. Dividend and profit remittance are constrained only by corporate-law solvency tests under the Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended) and, where applicable, dividend withholding tax (15% domestic rate; reduced under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable tax treaties). Cross-border flows are additionally screened under EU sanctions and AML/CTF rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation or mandatory currency-conversion obligation applies to Luxembourg service-export receipts, including study-abroad and visa-advisory fees. Foreign-currency proceeds may be retained in any currency; however, all cross-border payment instructions and account flows must be reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistical purposes and documented by the receiving bank for CSSF Regulation 12-02 AML/CFT compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for unlicensed, non-EEA offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK, Singapore, US platforms). Under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on payment services and the Law of 16 April 2009 on electronic money, only CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported EMIs may lawfully operate in Luxembourg. An EEA-licensed EMI (e.g., Estonia, Ireland, Germany) can supplement SWIFT rails for fee collection but cannot hold the SARL's capital-deposit or client-money escrow balances and should not serve as the principal corporate bank for this Medium-Risk Enhanced regulated activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Face-to-face attendance is not explicitly codified, but established bank practice under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and FATF Recommendation 10 requires at least one authorised manager or ultimate beneficial owner to appear in person at the bank during initial onboarding for a newly incorporated SARL with non-EU ownership. Remote opening is possible solely at the bank's discretion via eIDAS-qualified electronic signature, secure video identification and a pre-existing prime EU banking relationship; otherwise, physical interviews with two valid identity documents and a bound RCS excerpt (issued within the prior 3 months) are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-Risk Enhanced sector flag: migration/study-abroad services and international visa fee collection raise reputational exposure to irregular-migration, tuition-fraud and human-trafficking typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg business registration and statutory licence documentation for immigration-visa advisory; RCS commercial register extract (less than 3 months old); AML/CFT compliance manual aligned with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; designation of a qualified AML compliance officer; documented risk-based client onboarding procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or high-risk-jurisdiction exposure of UBOs; inbound funds originate from FATF grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP/sanctions screening reports (World-Check One, Dow Jones); certificate of tax residency for each UBO; sworn declaration of source of wealth; 12-month source-of-funds statements; external legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat; proof of specific transaction purpose linked to the study-abroad/visa mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payers (parents, overseas agencies, family offices) fund student tuition and visa fees, creating undisclosed-beneficiary red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised powers of attorney and signed payment mandates from each third-party payer; full KYC file on the underlying principal/student; reconciled wire-level payment schedule matched exactly to engagement contracts and fee invoices; anti-fraud verification of each upstream transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client-money mixing or unregulated escrow when advances from students are processed through the operational account rather than a segregated account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow and client-money segregation agreement with a Luxembourg credit institution; standard operating procedures for receipt and disbursement of client funds; quarterly independent accountant confirmations reconciling escrow balances to individual client commitments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value, front-loaded acceptance/visa fees with refundable-deposit structures trigger STR/CTR-type scrutiny and possible university-side reputational complaints.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed advisory and escrow agreements; documented commission-disclosure letters to partner universities; source-of-funds bank statements for each inbound payment; audited annual financial statements applying ISIC 7810 revenue recognition; an internal transaction log evidencing refund policy and timing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders transfer the fully paid-up SARL capital (minimum EUR 12,000) via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer to a dedicated capital-deposit account at a Luxembourg-licensed bank. Remittance instructions must state purpose code 'CAPT' (capital contribution) and the legal name of the shareholder/company. The bank issues a certificate of blocked funds ('attestation de blocage de fonds') in favour of the notary for incorporation under the Law of 10 August 1915; after RCS registration the funds are released to the operational account. All underlying shareholder identification documents and funding proof must be retained for at least 5 years under CSSF Regulation 12-02; any currency conversion of inbound capital is executed as an EUR spot purchase at the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border tuition, visa-application, embassy and overseas-agent payments, always carrying full beneficiary and remittance references ('TUITION/VISA/COMMISSION'); SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA counterparties; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) reserved for high-value performance-secured non-core disbursements. Each outbound payment must be pre-matched to the client escrow mandate, commission ledger and executed FX contract so as to avoid structuring flags; payments to universities and government immigration agencies are executed against documented admission and fee-invoice evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards (non-speculative, tenors up to 12 months, approved under board treasury policy)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for USD/INR, USD/CNY and other non-fully-convertible currencies relevant to tuition corridors
FX swaps (tom-next and roll) for escrow-funding gap management
European-style currency options (buy side only) for contingent visa-fee and tuition-fee exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Holding of the ordinary annual general meeting for approval of the annual accounts and discharge of the gerants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL; minutes recorded in the corporate minute book, no direct government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative strike-off for missing the AGM, but directors and gerants may incur civil liability; shareholders may apply to the competent court to convene the meeting, and the failure to approve the accounts blocks the statutory annual-accounts filing deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of the annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes and management report where applicable) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the shareholders and, in all cases, within seven months after the balance sheet date; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to judicial enforcement initiated by the Public Prosecutor, including a court-imposed astreinte (daily penalty payment) of approximately EUR 25 per day of continued default; repeated failure to file is a ground for judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off from the RCS after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual validation or summary statement of the RCS registration file (validation annuelle / état récapitulatif)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month immediately preceding the anniversary date of the company's initial RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to perform the annual validation triggers an LBR reminder; continued default after formal notice may result in suspension or closure of the RCS file and administrative strike-off of the SARL, with resulting loss of legal personality and standing to pursue legal rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and, where applicable, update of beneficial-owner data in the beneficial-owners register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership, including a share transfer, must be filed within one month of the change; absent changes, the SARL must perform the annual RBE confirmation by the anniversary of its RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, inaccurate filing, or late annual confirmation is an AML/register offence punishable by fines ranging from EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 for the legal entity, with possible additional daily penalty orders and criminal liability for responsible officers; persistent default can trigger regulatory sanctions and impede registration acts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three criteria on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Below these thresholds, audit is generally not compulsory unless required by the articles of association, a shareholders' resolution, a group audit obligation, or applicable sectoral rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial and annual accounts (transposing Directive 2013/EU/34), with consolidated accounts permitted to apply EU-adopted IFRS; supervised financial-services entities must also comply with CSSF requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain a current beneficial-owner file in the Luxembourg RBE and file any update within one month after a qualifying shareholding transfer or any other change. Additionally, the company must perform an annual RBE confirmation on the anniversary of its registration, confirming that the disclosed beneficial owners are complete, accurate, and unchanged; a transfer mid-year does not replace the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members (register of shares and shareholders)
Register of directors (gerants) and management decisions
Minute book of shareholders' meetings and board decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,300 - USD 11,000 per year if the statutory audit threshold is exceeded; nil for exempt small SARLs unless a voluntary audit is carried out

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax 6.75% for Luxembourg City; rates vary by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption under conditions), notional interest deduction on new equity, investment tax credit for certain assets, and R&D incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Corporate Income Tax and Municipal Business Tax combined) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (mandatory for companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end for electronic filing; extensions may be granted upon request. Provisional payments are due quarterly (10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: name, registered office, RCS number, tax ID.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must provide local PE details and appoint a tax representative.
State the PE's accounting period and currency (EUR).
Compute PE taxable income attributable to Luxembourg source activities, applying arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: tax losses carried forward, notional interest deduction, IP box relief, etc.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions applicable to the PE; provide supporting documentation.
Report any withholding tax credits or provisional payments made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions and transfer pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions; attach TP documentation if thresholds met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to EUR 1,000; late payment interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties up to 10% of tax due for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if parent holds ≥10% for ≥12 months; treaty rates may apply, e.g., 5% or 0% under many DTAs).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit Form 500 (withholding tax exemption/reduction request) to the Luxembourg tax authority (ACD) before payment, along with a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from the recipient's country, and evidence of beneficial ownership. For EU directive relief, provide a declaration of holding and compliance with anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on interest and royalties paid to non-residents under domestic law, except for certain cases (e.g., royalties to non-treaty countries at 15% if not exempt). Treaty rates may apply for interest (typically 0-10%) and royalties (typically 0-5%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000; Master File required if group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000; CbC Report required if group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for certain entities (e.g., IP holding, financing, leasing). For a consulting/immigration advisory SARL, substance is required to avoid being classified as a shell company: adequate premises, qualified employees, and actual decision-making in Luxembourg. Failure to demonstrate substance may lead to denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets in cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 200% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real substance (no office, no employees, no local management) while claiming treaty benefits or tax incentives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, additional tax assessments, and penalties up to 10% of tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for resulting tax liabilities if they failed to ensure substance; potential criminal charges for fraudulent misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining records for immigration/visa services involving large wire transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; regulatory bans from managing companies; seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for services or IP royalties that deviate from arm's length without proper documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 25% of the additional tax, and interest on underpayments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they approved the pricing; in severe cases, criminal charges for tax fraud.
